questions.question_en: With reference to the anti-defection law, consider the following statements: 1. The law specifies that a nominated member of a House can join a political party within six months of being appointed to the House. 2. The law does not mention the number of members of a legislature party that should give their 'assent' to a 'merger' of the original political party with another political party.
questions.language_status: English structured extraction; Telugu not included in index
questions.explanation_en: Reworded from UPSC CSP 2022 Q16; the answer here follows this wording (option 1). Under the Tenth Schedule a nominated member may join a party within six months of taking the seat, so statement 1 is correct; a merger needs the agreement of two-thirds of the legislature party, so statement 2 is wrong. Answer: option 1. Anti-defection law details need careful verification. The 10th Schedule specifies merger requires at least 2/3 of members.
questions.explanation_te: ఈ ప్రశ్న UPSC CSP 2022 Q16 నుంచి మార్చి రాసినది (reworded); ఇక్కడి జవాబు ఈ పాఠం ప్రకారమే (ఎంపిక 1). పదో షెడ్యూల్ (Tenth Schedule) ప్రకారం నామినేటెడ్ సభ్యుడు సభలో చేరిన ఆరు నెలల్లోపు ఏదైనా పార్టీలో చేరవచ్చు, కాబట్టి వాక్యం 1 సరైనది. విలీనం (merger)కు శాసనసభా పక్షంలో మూడింట రెండు వంతుల సభ్యుల అంగీకారం కావాలని చట్టం చెబుతుంది, కాబట్టి వాక్యం 2 తప్పు. జవాబు ఎంపిక 1.

key_audit.original_q: 1. The law specifies that a nominated legislator cannot join any political party within six months of being appointed to the House. 2. The law does not provide any time-frame within which the presiding officer has to decide a defection case. (a) 1 only (b) 2 only (c) Both (d) Neither
key_audit.note_en: Reworded from UPSC CSP 2022 Q16; the answer here follows this wording (option 1). Under the Tenth Schedule a nominated member may join a party within six months of taking the seat, so statement 1 is correct; a merger needs the agreement of two-thirds of the legislature party, so statement 2 is wrong. Answer: option 1.
